blocks.heading: What this section covers
blocks.text: Cover form, structure and language in the commentary, each tied to the audience it serves.

blocks.heading: The three grounds, in your own text
blocks.text: A commentary must cover form, structure and language, each tied to the audience it serves, because the brief was fulfilled by all three working together: the form found the reader, the structure carried them, the language held them. A commentary that covers one ground has described a third of the achievement — and the table rewards the whole.

blocks.heading: One ground is not enough
blocks.text: A commentary on structure alone, or on language alone, abandons two of the three grounds the table rewards: the piece was written with all three, and the commentary must account for all three. The error is common because language is the easiest ground to quote from; the cure is a plan with three headings before the writing starts — form, structure, language — and no heading left empty.

blocks.heading: Sharing the commentary out
blocks.text: A commentary is shared across form, structure and language by fixing them to choices: one paragraph on the form and its conventions (the greeting, the salutation, the report’s sections), one on the structure’s route (the opening’s promise, the order of the sections, the close), and one or two on the language’s work (the register, the imagery, the sentence shapes). The share is decided by where the choices sit: a piece with one striking image and a clever frame gives the image its sentence and the frame its own.

blocks.heading: Worked example: the three grounds found in one piece
blocks.text: Take the library report as the object. Its form choices: the title naming audience and subject, the numbered recommendations, the offer of a presentation — each one a decision about how the board is met. Its structure choices: findings before interpretation before recommendations, so the board receives evidence first and is led to action; the interpretation paragraph’s pivot (“not short of learners; short of room”) converts measurement into diagnosis. Its language choices: the exact figures, the quoted learner comment standing in the board’s papers, the costed recommendations. Three grounds, one piece, and a commentary that names a choice from each has covered the table’s whole ground.

blocks.heading: In the exam
blocks.text: The reflective commentary is Paper 2 Question 1(b), and it is worth ten marks for the analysis of your own Question 1(a) text: how its choices of form, structure and language fulfil the brief. The table rewards the same craft as the Paper 1 analysis questions — feature, evidence, effect, audience — with the brief in place of the context, and the same errors lose it: retelling, feature-listing, no quotation, one ground only. Write it in the analytical register, quote your own words, and keep every sentence pointed at the brief. The ten marks sit beside the fifteen of the piece, which makes the commentary a third of Section A’s total: twenty-five marks ride on one piece of writing and one account of its making, and the account is the cheaper half to learn, because it is the same analysis craft the rest of the qualification rewards.
